$comment: Source is TypeScript now (src/host/*.ts, src/client/*.ts), and every .ts file is type-checked unconditionally — `checkJs` only governs plain .js files, of which src/ has none. noImplicitAny is TRUE: the 536 implicit-any sites the migration left behind are all annotated, so the rule is now enforced by the compiler instead of by a ratchet (scripts/audit-implicit-any.mjs still runs, with a budget of 0, as a second opinion and as the place the trajectory is recorded). strictNullChecks is TRUE as well (via `strict`): the 99 sites it reported — 39 undefined-callable, and the rest null/index/assignability — are all settled, none of them with a `!`. Two of those were real bugs the flag surfaced: a request header that went out as the literal text "undefined" when a machine fingerprint was absent, and a `null` check-in notice that a `!== undefined` guard let through to a `.kind` read. `strict` also implies strictBindCallApply / strictFunctionTypes / noImplicitThis, all of which were already on individually. `erasableSyntaxOnly` is TRUE and is the one flag here that exists for the TEST harness rather than for the types: the suite runs on bare `node --test` with no bundler and no dependencies, importing `src/host/*.ts` and the client's rule layer (`card-model.ts`, `controller.ts`) directly, so Node's strip-only loader is the real compiler for everything a test can reach. Strip-only mode cannot execute `enum`, `namespace`, parameter properties (`constructor(private x)`) or angle-bracket assertions (`<T>expr`), and it fails at RUNTIME with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX — but plain tsc accepts all four, so without this flag a `.ts` file can typecheck clean and only explode when the suite runs it. The flag turns that discipline into a compile-time error (TS1294). It costs nothing today because the sources are already fully erasable; the ambient `declare namespace JSX` in `src/client/react-shim.d.ts` is a declaration, not a runtime namespace, and is unaffected. This is also the line that decides which extension a file may use: anything a bare-Node test imports must be `.ts`; `.tsx` is for the render layer, which no test imports directly (Node cannot execute `.tsx` under any flag). Run it with `npm run typecheck`.
